criterion: Every tip at the foot of the loading screen speaks about the world of the game rather than about a control of the interface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each of the six tips describes the world, the travellers or the journey. No if any tip explains a button, a panel or another piece of the interface.

criterion: Picking up Canon or Super canon in Le Vol sends a banner across the screen that holds and then leaves.
evaluation_rule: Yes if both weapons raise a banner that crosses, holds and leaves. No if a weapon arrives silently or the banner stays on screen.

criterion: The sound set is a music bed, the sea, the wind, one click and two footsteps, the footstep following the ground under the character and the sea swelling toward the shore as the wind rises on high open ground.
evaluation_rule: Yes if those six sources are present and the footstep, the sea and the wind answer the ground and the place. No if a seventh source appears or the sea and the wind hold one flat level everywhere.

criterion: The whole page reads as the portfolio of one creative developer built as a game, the maker's work standing in the landscape as an orchard, a lighthouse, a ski run and a flight through a wind portal.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the four pieces of work are places in one landscape and the visitor meets them by walking. No if the work is listed as projects, cards or a menu of links.

criterion: The palette holds five colours with one transparency: a near-black document ground, a loading ground one step lighter, a mid soft orange kept for paper things, and two blues, one mid and vivid, one deep and muted.
evaluation_rule: Yes if those five colours and the single transparency carry the whole interface and the orange appears only on paper things. No if a sixth colour appears or the orange is used for text and panels of other kinds.

criterion: The music bed is detuned tones under a moving filter, the sea rising and falling about every twelve seconds, the wind level following how exposed the character stands, the click a short high tone, the snow footstep brighter and longer than the grass footstep, and repeated sounds pooled so that fast footsteps keep up.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each of those sound sources behaves as described over a minute of walking. No if the music is a fixed loop, the sea holds one level or fast footsteps stall.

criterion: The social preview image is rendered from the home camera at build time.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the preview image shows the home composition as the home camera frames it. No if the preview is a hand-drawn graphic, a logo card or a photograph of something else.

criterion: The flight display declares a colour block of its own, the filled and empty life cells swapping colours, the tallies two units in from the bottom corners and the life strip one unit in from the right edge.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the flight display holds its own deep slate, pale ice blue and white and sits at those margins. No if the flight display borrows the site colours or drifts from those corners.

criterion: Touch buttons are translucent white circles with a thin white edge and glyphs at half the button size, the stick twice the size of a button.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the touch controls are drawn that way on a sideways phone. No if the buttons are opaque squares, carry labels in words or match the stick in size.

criterion: Dragging anywhere on the home composition swings the camera around the cottage, and the camera lifts off the hill into a bright sky as the welcome screen arrives.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the drag turns the home scene and the camera climbs on the way to the welcome screen. No if the home scene holds one fixed view or the welcome screen cuts in over a still picture.

criterion: The first zone begins streaming during the home screen, the world stays drawn behind the second wait, and walking begins as soon as that first zone is ready.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the second wait is short because the first zone arrived early and the world is visible behind the wait. No if the whole world downloads before the visitor may move or the second wait covers a blank page.

criterion: The character is pushed along the ground and up the slopes, and talk ranges and pickup ranges live in that same physical world.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the character climbs and descends with the ground and a prompt arrives by standing close in the world. No if the character slides through the ground, jumps to a place at once or picks things up from a fixed screen distance.

criterion: In the world the camera stays above the height at which the camera looks, glides toward position at a pace that holds on a fast machine and a slow one, and lifts the gaze a little as the camera pulls back.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the camera holds those three rules through a walk across a slope. No if the camera sinks under the look height, snaps to position or keeps one gaze angle at every distance.

criterion: Walking into a fruit in La Cueillette picks the fruit, an apple counting as Pommes, a banana as Bananes and a golden fruit as Bonus, and touching a rotten fruit costs one apple down to zero.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each fruit lands in its own tally and a rotten fruit takes one apple away, holding at zero. No if fruit is picked by a button press, the tallies mix or the apple tally falls under zero.

criterion: Turning the beam in La Veille du Phare guides ships between the reefs, a ship brought through counting as Navires guidés and a storm ridden out as Tempêtes traversées.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the beam steers the ships and both outcomes reach their own tally. No if the ships steer themselves or one outcome is counted for the other.

criterion: A ski run ends at the finish line or after 120 seconds, and a flight run counts a target hit as Cibles touchées, a cannon as Canons trouvés and a ring as Anneaux traversés, ending as the last life cell is lost or after 120 seconds.
evaluation_rule: Yes if both runs end on either of their two conditions and the flight tallies answer the three pickups. No if a run carries on past the clock or a pickup lands in the wrong tally.

criterion: The first finished orchard run raises a rope bridge between Le Promontoire and Le Bois Murmurant.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the bridge stands after the first orchard run and the crossing becomes walkable. No if the bridge is there from the start or the gap stays open after a finished run.

criterion: The quality choice in the Menu settings carries the depth blur and the glow at Haute and drops both at Basse, and sets the grass draw distance and the shadow sharpness with the same turn.
evaluation_rule: Yes if moving between Basse and Haute changes the blur, the glow, the grass distance and the shadow edge. No if the picture looks the same at both ends of the choice.

criterion: The boards stay quick with tens of thousands of entries behind them and with a few hundred viewers holding boards open, and the world keeps pace after a long session of opening and closing layers.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the board answers quickly under that load and the frame rate holds after many layers have opened and closed. No if the board slows as entries pile up or the world degrades over a long session.

criterion: A pointer drag in the world swings the camera freely as the character stands still and weakens about a hundred times over as the character walks, and the mouse wheel pulls the camera in and out.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the same drag turns the view far while standing and barely at all while walking, and the wheel changes the distance. No if the drag has one strength at all times or the wheel does nothing.

criterion: Some routes through the world stay hidden until a look into the corners of a zone finds them.
evaluation_rule: Yes if searching a corner of a zone opens a way the main path leaves out. No if every route is visible from the arrival point of its zone.

criterion: Screen state, character position and collection live as layers over one running world, each layer sitting at its own named place in one ordered stack, and a panel reads the game state rather than driving the world.
evaluation_rule: Yes if every screen is a layer over the same world and closing a layer returns the visitor where the visitor stood. No if a screen replaces the world, restarts it or drives the world from inside a panel.

criterion: The receipt is a centred paper panel and the one region that scrolls, scrolling once the receipt stands taller than nine tenths of the window.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a long receipt scrolls inside its own panel and the rest of the page holds still. No if the whole page scrolls or a long receipt is cut off.

criterion: In the home composition a tree leans in from the left out of focus beside a row of trees along a flat sea under a deep blue sky, warm spots of light drift over the grass, and only the cottage and the tiny figure in front of the porch are sharp.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the home scene holds that depth, those drifting lights and that single sharp subject. No if the whole scene is in focus or the foreground tree and the sea are missing.

criterion: Every letter of the home title and its subtitle carries a soft shadow, and interface text over the world holds a contrast of at least four and a half to one against the brightest pixel behind the text.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the letters carry a shadow and the text stays readable over the brightest part of the world. No if the shadow is missing or the text washes out over a bright sky.

criterion: The welcome paragraph standing before the second load holds a reading measure of about half the window width.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the welcome lines run to roughly half the window. No if the paragraph runs the full width or sits in a narrow column of a third or less.

criterion: The character is folded card in a wide conical hat with a satchel at the hip and visible facets, the cottage is paper planks and paper shingles in a warm sand colour, trees are crumpled paper trunks carrying many separately made leaves, the grass is real blades bright at the tip and dark at the root, and two grey rocks with chalk drawings lie at the arrival point on Le Promontoire.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the world is built from those paper forms and the rocks stand at the arrival point. No if the world uses smooth photographic surfaces or the described pieces are missing.

criterion: A pill fills from the bottom edge to the top on pointer rest or keyboard focus with the label flipping colour, the pill fills dark with a light label on the receipt and board panels, and dialogue choice buttons drop the outline.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the fill climbs from the bottom on both pointer rest and focus and the panel pills read dark with a light label. No if the fill arrives as a flat colour change or the dialogue choices keep an outline.

criterion: The key ring is a thin circle on the edge of a box one-and-a-half times the label size with the letter a centred capital, and the ring turns dark as a pill fills light behind the ring.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the ring holds that shape and flips with the pill behind the ring. No if the ring is a square badge, holds a lower-case letter or keeps one colour through the fill.

criterion: The Menu control is two interlocking paper gears turning slowly in the light of the world sun, the notebook control is a paper satchel with a handle at twice the size of the gears, and both redraw only on a change.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the two corner controls are those drawn objects and hold still until something changes. No if the corners carry flat icons or redraw every frame.

criterion: The dialogue shadow is a gradient from almost black at the bottom to transparent over a plain black fallback, and each dialogue line and each dialogue button carries a soft drop shadow.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the gradient stands behind the dialogue and the lines carry their own soft shadow. No if the dialogue sits on a solid band or the text reads flat against the world.

criterion: Models are simple shapes with faceted surfaces in one flat paper material, lit by a warm key light from one side and a cool fill light from the other, under a generated sky gradient that runs from deep blue above to a warm pale horizon with a softened sun, with faceted tree trunks carrying leaf cards in three greens and water rippling between a deep and a mid blue-green with a sun highlight.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the world holds that flat faceted material, that two-light setup, that sky and that water. No if the world uses photographic textures, one flat light or a plain blue water plane.

criterion: The world carries depth of field, a soft glow on the bright spots and a colour grade held as data, and the counter silhouettes are collected models rendered once and crushed to black.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the picture holds that depth, glow and grade and the receipt silhouettes are the game objects in black. No if the world renders flat or the silhouettes are drawn shapes of another kind.

criterion: Title letters write out one at a time, each letter settling from slightly right and slightly large, and the Voyager pill fades up from slightly below and settles late on purpose.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the letters arrive one by one and the way in settles after the title has finished. No if the title appears at once or the way in arrives with the first letter.

criterion: A found object stops the world under a translucent black wash with two star-bursts turning in opposite tints, one behind the other, and the object turns in front of the visitor as a rendered model before landing in the notebook.
evaluation_rule: Yes if finding an object holds the world, turns the model and records the find in the notebook. No if a found object shows as a flat icon or leaves the notebook untouched.

criterion: The tally swells on a gain and shudders back to its place on a loss, the swell scaling up then settling and the shudder ending where the shudder started, and the clock pulses gently over the last ten seconds in a smaller, slower, repeating beat.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a gain, a loss and the last ten seconds each carry their own movement. No if the numbers change with no movement at all.

criterion: The change-over wipe between layers is near-black and takes the pointer for as long as the wipe shows.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the wipe covers the change in near-black and swallows clicks underneath. No if the change happens with a white flash or clicks land on the layer behind the wipe.

criterion: A layer fade and a layer rise follow one number, an entrance interrupted halfway reverses smoothly, the board rises a little, the notebook rises a whole page height, bottom-docked things park twice their height below the window, and the interface keeps to the four eased speeds of the set.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the layers share one timing, reverse cleanly halfway and travel those distances. No if a layer jumps, sticks halfway or carries a bespoke curve of its own.

criterion: The Contact hairline on the home screen grows outward from the middle.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the rule under the contact word opens from the centre toward both ends. No if the rule wipes in from one side or is simply there.

criterion: The hat brim of the world character lags a moment behind the head, walking swings the legs with counter-swinging arms, and running widens the arc as the torso pitches forward.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the character carries that lag and those two gaits. No if the character slides along with a rigid pose.

criterion: Under a reduced-motion preference the clock warning and the own-row glow stand still, the star-burst stops and the layers cross-fade in place, and the camera and the character keep moving.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the decorative movement stops under that preference and the world still walks. No if the decorative movement carries on or the camera and the character freeze with the rest.

criterion: Sound begins at the first press of the visitor, and the whole world stays playable in silence.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the page is silent until the first press and every part of the world can be played with the sound muted. No if sound starts on arrival or a mute leaves some action unreachable.

criterion: A found object is announced as Objet trouvé, followed by the object name, and a tally change is announced as the item label, a comma and the count.
evaluation_rule: Yes if both announcements reach the live region in that shape. No if the announcements are missing or read as a sentence of another wording.

criterion: The focus ring stays legible over the bright and the dark parts of the world by shape as much as by colour, every pointer-rest state has a matching focus state, and every meaning carried by a colour is carried by a second cue.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the ring reads over a bright sky and a dark wood and each hover state answers a focus state. No if the ring disappears over one of them or a state is told by colour alone.

criterion: On a wide window the home title sits near a ninth of the height with Voyager in the lower third and Contact at the bottom edge, and on a narrow window the title sits a tenth of the way down.
evaluation_rule: Yes if both windows place the title, the way in and the contact word at those heights. No if the composition holds one fixed layout at every width.

criterion: Below the breakpoint the dialogue text grows against the root size and the lighthouse and ski rows draw in toward the edge as those displays shrink further than the rest of the interface.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the dialogue reads larger against the root and the game rows tighten on a narrow window. No if every part shrinks by the same amount.

criterion: A phone held upright is asked to rotate rather than given a cramped layout, and the loading figure stays centred at three tenths of the height on a laptop window and on a phone window.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the upright phone shows the rotate ask and the loading figure holds that height on both machines. No if an upright phone gets a squeezed layout or the figure drifts with the window.

criterion: A paper-coloured ellipse carrying LOADING stands before the figure renders, the figure fading in over the ellipse, and the tips crossfade in one place with a drawn keyboard beside the first tip and a drawn controller beside the second.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the ellipse holds the first frame and the tips change in place with those two drawings. No if the first frame is blank or a tip change moves the layout.

criterion: Keys A and D swing the camera, the keypad zooms in and out, holding Shift runs, the left stick and the directional pad walk, the right stick swings and zooms, and a controller carrying another axis order is read through a per-device mapping table.
evaluation_rule: Yes if each of those keys and sticks reaches the action named for the key or the stick, whatever controller is plugged in. No if a controller with another axis order steers the camera the wrong way or a key does nothing.

criterion: The forward page control tilts and grows the label as the arrow slides, the back control tilts the other way as the arrow grows, and an openable page item swells a little with a hairline drawn from the middle outward.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the two page controls answer a pointer in those opposite ways and the openable items swell under a pointer. No if both controls move alike or the page items hold still.

criterion: An open dialogue covers the Menu control in the corner of the world.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the dialogue or its shadow sits over the corner control. No if the corner control stays reachable through every dialogue.

criterion: The corner controls keep redrawing behind an open panel that hides them.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the hidden surfaces carry on drawing frames behind a panel. No if a hidden surface stops until the surface is shown again.

criterion: Interface text stands over the brightest parts of the world at a contrast under the readable floor.
evaluation_rule: Yes if any interface text drops under four and a half to one against the brightest pixel behind the text. No if every piece of interface text holds that floor.

criterion: A tip on the loading screen explains a control of the interface instead of describing the world.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a tip names a button, a panel or a setting. No if all six tips stay inside the fiction of the world.
